title: A Harvest for the Smile
premise: When Elodie Eriksen returns to his grandmother's decaying farmhouse to bury his twin brother Anders, he discovers the funeral was for the wrong sibling—Anders is still alive, or something wearing him is. The house's photographs keep changing, each one now showing an extra chair at the kitchen table, a chair that wasn't there before and that no one else can see. Digging through grandma's letters, Elodie learns that in 1974 she made a bargain with something in the orchard: a life given every fifty years in exchange for the family's survival, and this year the debt has come due. To end it, Elodie must return what was taken—a name, buried under the apple trees—and accept that doing so will cost him either his brother, himself, or the found family of neighbors who have quietly kept him alive. In the end, Elodie gives back the stolen name, dissolving the bargain, but the final photograph shows the extra chair empty at last—and Elodie gone from it.
about_author: Ines Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate sales in rural Scandinavia, where she developed an obsession with unclaimed photographs. She writes horror about houses that remember more than the people who live in them.

chapters.title: The Wrong Brother
chapters.summary: Elodie arrives at the farmhouse for Anders's funeral, numb and counting doors out of old habit. At the wake, a neighbor swears she saw Anders last week, alive. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: grief curdling into dread as the ground shifts under what he believes.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Doors
chapters.summary: Elodie catalogs the house to steady himself and finds every door accounted for except one: a narrow door behind the pantry wallpaper that doesn't appear on any blueprint. Grandma's cat refuses to enter the kitchen. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the comfort of ritual failing against a house that lies.

chapters.title: An Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Sorting photographs for the memorial, Elodie notices a wooden chair at the kitchen table in pictures spanning sixty years—a chair that isn't in the room. In the newest photos it sits closer to the camera. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: quiet horror; the past is being edited.

chapters.title: Marta Knows Things
chapters.summary: Neighbor Marta Halvorsen brings casseroles and warnings, revealing she and her late mother 'kept count' for grandma too. She won't come inside after dark. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: the first hint of found family—and that Elodie was never meant to face this alone.

chapters.title: Letters from 1974
chapters.summary: In grandma's locked writing desk, Elodie finds correspondence with a man named Verner about 'the arrangement' and an orchard harvest that never reached market. The last letter is torn in half. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as debt rather than gift.

chapters.title: A Phone Call from Anders
chapters.summary: Elodie's phone rings from his dead brother's number. Anders's voice asks why Elodie came home, says 'you shouldn't have,' and mentions the chair by name. The call traces to inside the house. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into guilt—he was summoned.

chapters.title: The Orchard at Night
chapters.summary: Following scratch marks on the pantry door, Elodie walks the overgrown orchard and finds one tree still bearing fruit out of season, its roots wrapped around something rectangular. He doesn't dig. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: temptation and restraint; some inheritances should stay buried.

chapters.title: What Marta's Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Marta shares her mother's notebook: decades of tallies, names crossed out every fiftieth year, ending with 'E. Eriksen — 2024.' Her mother died keeping the count. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: grief mirrored; two families bound by the same silence.

chapters.title: The Chair Moves
chapters.summary: Elodie wakes to find the extra chair beside his bed, warm to the touch, smelling of apples and pond water. Every photograph in the house now shows someone sitting in it, face turned away. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: invasion—the invisible thing wants to be acknowledged.

chapters.title: Verner's Half Letter
chapters.summary: In the parish archive, Elodie finds Verner Ostrand vanished in 1974, the same year grandma's farm miraculously survived bankruptcy and blight. The torn letter's missing half is in the archive: 'It does not want blood. It wants to be remembered rightly.' POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Doors That Weren't There Yesterday
chapters.summary: The house begins rearranging itself; hallways lengthen, rooms repeat, and the pantry door appears in three places at once. Elodie marks every threshold and loses count anyway. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: loss of control; the house is herding him toward the orchard.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing My Brother
chapters.summary: Anders appears at the fence line, solid and wrong—smiling a half-second too long, reciting family memories slightly misordered. He asks Elodie to let him in. Elodie counts the doors instead and keeps them shut. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the trap wears love's face.

chapters.title: Grandma's Confession
chapters.summary: A hidden tape reveals grandma's voice: in 1974 she didn't sacrifice a stranger—she took Verner's name and gave it to the orchard thing, binding it as family so it would protect them. 'I stole a son,' she says, 'and it has been waiting to be given back.' POV: Elodie listening. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; grandma was both savior and thief.

chapters.title: Keeping Count Together
chapters.summary: Marta moves in temporarily, and the two build a fragile routine—meals, tallies, salt lines—that makes the house almost bearable. For one evening, it feels like family. Then all the clocks stop at 7:14, the minute Verner disappeared. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: warmth as counterweight; what they stand to lose.

chapters.title: The Harvest Begins
chapters.summary: Out-of-season apples ripen overnight across the whole orchard, heavy and sweet-rotten. Every neighbor within a mile dreams of sitting in the extra chair. Marta's tally book fills itself with fresh ink. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: escalation; the debt is collecting interest from everyone.

chapters.title: Digging Up 1974
chapters.summary: Elodie excavates beneath the fruiting tree and finds a child's coffin-sized box containing Verner's belongings, a mirror, and a name written on birch bark. Touching the bark, he hears Verner's voice say thank you. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: sorrow; the monster was a person first.

chapters.title: The Price Named Twice
chapters.summary: The house traps Elodie in the pantry-door space, where the thing offers terms: give back the name and lose your own place in every photograph, or refuse and it takes Marta as the new keeper. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the cruelest choice—erasure versus sacrificing the family he just found.

chapters.title: What Anders Would Have Done
chapters.summary: Elodie finds Anders alive, drugged and hidden in a care facility an hour away—grandma stashed him there years ago as insurance. Anders, lucid for once, tells Elodie not to trade himself: 'You were always the one who counted. Let me be counted instead.' POV: Anders. Emotional beat: twin bond reclaimed; love as strategy, not sacrifice theater.

chapters.title: The Return
chapters.summary: At moonrise, Elodie, Anders, and Marta hold a rite at the tree: speaking Verner's true name, returning the birch bark, and naming the thing as family no longer. The orchard screams in forty years of held breath. The extra chair appears between them, occupied by a thin man weeping. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: climax; restitution as exorcism.

chapters.title: Fifty Years of Hunger, Ended
chapters.summary: Verner's ghost, freed, unbinds the bargain—but the debt demands a keeper's name to close the ledger. Before Elodie can offer his, Marta writes her family name into the book and burns it, ending the keeper line entirely. The house exhales; the false doors seal forever. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: costly grace; survival finally paid in full.

chapters.title: The Last Photograph
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the farmhouse is sold. The final photo from that autumn shows the kitchen table, the extra chair empty at last—and where Elodie stood, only light. But Elodie, alive and unnamed in the picture, stands outside the frame, choosing to be seen on his own terms. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: bittersweet release; invisibility traded for freedom.

chapters.title: A Harvest for the Smile
chapters.summary: Spring: Elodie, Anders, and Marta plant a new orchard where the old one burned back, leaving one wild tree standing. They set a fourth chair at their table—for Verner, for grandma, for whoever comes next. When the wind moves the leaves, it sounds almost like counting. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: resolution; inheritance transformed from debt into remembrance.
